text:
Priya M: heads up — onboarding new hf/zenith-4 model hit a weird failure during our redwood conversion. fast tokenizer produced tokens but the slow loader complains about missing tokenizer_config.json and special tokens mismatch.
Aaron L: can you paste the error?
Priya M: sure — error from slow tokenizer: 
```
ValueError: 'unk_token' not found in tokenizer_config.json (expected '<unk>')
Looking for tokenizer_config.json at /mnt/models/zenith-4/tokenizer_config.json — file not found.
Falling back to slow tokenizer failed.
```
Priya M: fast tokenizer ships tokenizer.json and vocab.json only (HF Fast). our hf-to-redwood-convert picked up tokenizer.json and wrote fast artifacts, but we don't generate a tokenizer_config.json for slow fallback.
Cami Z: ohhh classic fast-vs-slow mismatch. HF sometimes stores specials in both places but not guaranteed. did the original HF repo have tokenizers/tokenizer_config.json?
Priya M: upstream only has tokenizer.json + special_tokens_map.json in the repo root, no tokenizer_config.json. special_tokens_map.json lists cls, sep, pad but keys are "cls_token" vs the slow loader expects "cls_token_type_id" in config — mismatch.
Aaron L: quick patch options: (1) generate tokenizer_config.json during convert by merging special_tokens_map.json into a minimal config, (2) teach our slow-loader to consume special_tokens_map.json if tokenizer_config.json absent, (3) canonicalize at load time: prefer tokenizer.json for all cases.
Jihoon K: option 1 seems lowest risk. we already generate merge metadata for quantization. a tiny JSON writer: 
```bash
python - <<PY
import json,sys
root='${MODEL_PATH}'
with open(root+'/special_tokens_map.json') as f:
    s=json.load(f)
cfg={'unk_token': s.get('unk_token','<unk>'), 'pad_token': s.get('pad_token','<pad>'), 'cls_token': s.get('cls_token','<cls>')}
open(root+'/tokenizer_config.json','w').write(json.dumps(cfg))
PY
```
Priya M: nice. also saw an eval regression in quantized run: answers truncated more often when we fallback to slow; probably because slow tokenizer's special tokens differ so prefix cache logic breaks. the regression popped in the quant-8bit runs.
Cami Z: worth adding a CI check: after conversion run a 100-sample tokenization parity test between fast and slow tokens. fail conversion if >1% mismatch.
Aaron L: agreed. I'll add a small test in hf-to-redwood-convert: run `python -m redwood.token.check_parity --model PATH --samples 100` and emit error code.
Priya M: also, small gotcha — some repos use `tokenizer.json` with merged specials, but `special_tokens_map.json` keys are nested under "additional_special_tokens" sometimes. script needs to deep-handle all variants.
Jihoon K: I'll update the conversion PR with: (a) generator for tokenizer_config.json, (b) parity test, (c) unit that logs when special token canonical names differ and prints mapping.
infra-bot: deploy-preview created for branch fix/tokenizer-config-gen -> preview-245 (will run convert pipeline against zenith-4). :rocket:
Priya M: thanks. quick manual workaround for folks hitting this: in model dir drop a tiny tokenizer_config.json with unk/pad/cls keys (see snippet) and restart onboarding.
Aaron L: filing a doc blurb in the conversion README about fast vs slow pitfalls and the parity test.
Cami Z: can we also add a one-off migration that re-runs convert on existing models older than 2025-01-01 to catch orphans? we saw a few orphans in the dedicated pools.
Jihoon K: yes — I'll add a cron job to kick convert for models missing tokenizer_config.json and tag them. log will be in infra-models-migration.
Priya M: great. leaving notes in the model ticket and marking the ticket as blocker for zenith-4 onboard until parity passes. :eyes:
Aaron L: lgtm, thanks team.
Priya M: thanks — will follow up with the conversion PR link when ready.
